value.overview: The Amethyst-throated Mountain-gem is a tiny nectar-feeding bird with rapid wingbeats, hovering flight, and iridescent color. Field recognition often comes from large hummingbird shape, strong bill, and iridescent throat color. It is found around flower-rich forest edge, gardens, canyons, scrub, open woodland, riparian areas, and feeders. In Canada, its status can be common, local, seasonal, or rare depending on the province and season, so current sightings remain important for trip planning.
value.classification: The Amethyst-throated Mountain-gem (Lampornis amethystinus) belongs to the family Hummingbirds in the order Apodiformes. This is the practical birding classification for quick field reference.
value.identification: Look for large hummingbird shape, strong bill, and iridescent throat color. Also use size, posture, bill shape, flight style, voice, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
value.rangeHabitat: It is tied to flower-rich habitats and tiny insect prey. In Canada, hummingbird occurrence is highly regional; some are regular in the west or at feeders, while others are rare visitors.
value.migrationStatus: Mostly migratory or seasonally mobile in North America, though some coastal populations can remain year-round where winters are mild and food is available.
value.breeding: It builds a tiny cup nest of plant down, lichens, and spider silk on a branch or sheltered perch. The female handles most nesting duties. Clutches are usually two white eggs.
value.dietFeeding: It feeds on nectar and catches tiny insects and spiders for protein. It may use feeders, but natural flowers and insect-rich habitat remain important.
value.behavior: It is energetic and often territorial around flowers or feeders. It hovers, darts, chases rivals, and may perform courtship display flights. Small size does not mean gentle behavior.
